introduction: The final capstone starts with users and consequences, not a diagram of every tool you learned. Taskboard needs a small product brief: who uses it, what data matters, expected load, failure impact and who will operate it.

Choose one primary deployment platform. Retain the second cloud as your earlier tested portability exercise; active-active complexity is optional and needs an actual requirement. Local execution is valid, but it supports local claims only.

Define acceptance before building. A measurable target includes workload, observation window, measurement method and response when it is missed. A five-minute test cannot prove a monthly availability promise.
prerequisites: Earlier release, restore, performance and security evidence, including known gaps.
Your learner repository at ~/dev-opps-lab. No new cloud resources are required this week.
If choosing a cloud target later, use the earlier account/project/region and cost-inventory procedures before creating anything.

concepts.title: Requirements define adequate engineering
paragraphs: Specify users, operations, data sensitivity and consequences of failure. A private learning service with synthetic data differs from a public customer system. Public Taskboard requires replacing teaching tokens with an established identity provider and reviewed verification of issuer, audience, expiry and ownership.
Separate functional requirements from reliability/security/operability constraints. Every major control should point to a requirement or threat, not simply a tool you want to showcase.
concepts.example: A requirement to recover yesterday's completed tasks implies retained usable backups; a requirement to keep tasks private implies server-enforced identity and ownership.
concepts.judgment: No architecture is universally production-ready. State which users, workload, threat and budget make your design adequate.

concepts.title: An SLO needs a denominator and a window
paragraphs: A service-level indicator is a measured quantity such as successful valid task requests divided by valid task requests. An objective adds a target and observation window. Include failures that matter to users rather than only healthy infrastructure samples.

Latency should name operation, dataset, concurrency, warmup and fault intervals. RTO/RPO need a known recovery scenario. A cost ceiling needs inventory and an owner who reacts before or when it is exceeded.
concepts.example: 99.5% valid-request success over 28 days is an example objective, not something a five-minute lab demonstrates.
concepts.judgment: Targets are hypotheses to test. Adjust them through a recorded product/risk decision, never quietly after a failed test.

steps.title: 1 · Write a concrete service brief
steps.purpose: Use an editable baseline and replace assumptions with your actual choice.

commands.code:
cd ~/dev-opps-lab
mkdir -p evidence/capstone
cat > evidence/capstone/service-brief.md <<'MD'
# Taskboard service brief
Users: small private learning team; synthetic tasks only.
Operations: create, list, read, complete; API contract1.0.
Primary platform: local Compose for this baseline; replace only with a justified chosen target.
Secondary cloud: retain earlier portability evidence, not mandatory active-active operation.
Dataset: at most1000 tasks per identity; larger workloads require pagination/resource-limit design.
Workload:10 clients,90% reads/10% completions,60s warmup/300s sample.
Latency hypothesis: p95 below300ms under the stated local conditions; report errors/p99 too.
Availability: define a valid-request indicator and a28day objective; lab evidence cannot establish that window.
Recovery target: RTO30min/RPO24h for the declared daily-logical-backup scenario.
Exposure: loopback/private tunnel only; synthetic tokens are not public authentication.
Cost boundary: no additional cloud spend for local baseline; account for local disk/power/time.
Owners: name application, infrastructure, security-review and incident responsibilities.
Unmet controls: list every missing item before calling the release ready.
MD
cat evidence/capstone/service-brief.md
explain: The quoted heredoc creates a reviewable starting brief, not an automatic pass. Edit users, owners, targets and platform based on actual evidence.
The fixed workload preserves the course benchmark. Cost0 means no additional cloud resources here, not literally free hardware/energy.
commands.expected: A bounded service promise and visible assumptions.

steps.title: 2 · Translate promises into acceptance evidence

commands.code:
cat > evidence/capstone/acceptance.md <<'MD'
# Acceptance contract
Behavior: unit, realPostgres integration and realHTTP system reports; no skipped core cases.
Privacy: missing/invalididentity denied; cross-owner reads/completions404; denied update leaves state unchanged.
Reliability: bounded dependency503, readiness503/liveness200, committed task survives app/DB restarts.
Recovery: separate destination; IDs/owners/titles/completion match; measuredRTO/RPO.
Delivery: source commit, immutable tested image, config revision and schema history trace together.
Security: scan triage, trusted artifact policy and scoped expiring exceptions.
Operations: user-oriented telemetry, clear runbooks, current cost inventory and named owners.
Handoff: another operator or labeled fresh-environment self-review can rebuild/deploy/recover.
Decision: failed mandatory condition blocks release; exceptions require owner/scope/expiry and must not hide critical data/privacy failures.
MD
explain: Each row names an observation and retained evidence rather than an adjective such as robust.
Core identity/data controls are mandatory; a high score elsewhere cannot compensate for a known cross-user data leak.
commands.troubleshoot: Check the working directory with pwd, then read the first failing command before changing configuration.

steps.checkpoint: Map each check to an actual report or mark it incomplete.

steps.title: 3 · Challenge one assumption before committing to complexity
steps.purpose: Analyze a tenfold workload increase without secretly changing the contract.

commands.code:
cat > evidence/capstone/assumption-challenge.md <<'MD'
# Tenfold workload challenge
Current limit:1000 tasks per identity; list is unpaginated.
Changed need:10000 tasks per identity and100 concurrent users.
What fails first? Form a hypothesis using query, connection, response-size and memory evidence.
Contract decision: design pagination and limits before claiming this workload is supported.
Capacity decision: compare measured bottleneck improvement with extra replicas/DB connection budget.
Risk: retries can amplify overload; creation is not idempotent.
Decision record: retain current bounded scope or approve a separately versioned extension with new tests.
MD
git status --short
explain: Write the changed requirement and its consequences. Do not load-test the unsupported dataset and label any accidental success production scalability.
git status helps prepare a reviewed change to the brief/acceptance record.

questions.hint: What extra requirement does a second active platform satisfy?
questions.answer: It reduces operating and failure complexity unless a concrete need justifies multiple active systems. Portability evidence can remain a separate exercise.

questions.prompt: Can five successful minutes prove a monthly SLO?
questions.answer: No. The sample supports behavior under stated conditions, not availability across unseen failures, updates and traffic for a month.

questions.hint: Are synthetic tokens an identity platform?
questions.answer: Adopt established identity-provider integration with maintained issuer/audience/expiry verification and proven ownership; review privacy, abuse, network and operating requirements for real users.

exercise.brief: Review the brief as a skeptical customer and identify three unmet requirements.
constraints: Separate assumptions, measured facts and proposed targets.
deliverables: Threat model, acceptance mapping and primary-platform decision record.
acceptance: Every major control traces to need/threat.
Operating budget and ownership are explicit.
hints: Challenge data sensitivity, tenfold traffic, zone loss or a leaked credential.
solution: Choose the simplest platform that meets the stated need, preserve evidence for alternatives, and turn gaps into acceptance work before building.

explain: Keep planning artifacts for the capstone. No resources were created.

repoConnections.principle: Review capabilities rather than collecting tools
repoConnections.application: Use a second roadmap to check balance among software practice, systems, delivery, cloud, security and operations. Turn missing evidence into a specific exercise, such as restoration or denied access. Do not add a platform just because it appears on another map. Requirements and observed weaknesses decide the next work. Practice: During quarterly review, choose one weak capability, define an acceptance check and complete it before adding optional tooling.

Define a useful user action and measure success within a meaningful latency threshold. An SLO states the target over a window; an error budget describes allowed bad events. This makes release tradeoffs explicit. Alert on actionable conditions, write symptom runbooks and examine contributing conditions after incidents. Practice: Define a Taskboard SLI from success counts and latency. Calculate good/total from a sample, inject a brief failure and connect the alert to a runbook.

notes: Commands and configurations are supplied for the stated disposable lab. Authoring host has no operational Docker/WSL; container, database and cluster exercises are not claimed executed. Record your own outputs before passing a gate.
